what_it_does: Creates one record, sleeps 2 s, then checks find_data_objects time-offset filters against the record age, so the sleep sets the age the asserts require.

decisions.label: a
decisions.why: The sleep is idle wait, which draws little energy, and the asserts need the record to be more than 100 ms old, so the sleep only sets a floor on that age. Shortening it changes wall-clock time, not energy.

what_it_does: Runs two fresh python3 subprocesses that import dxpy and print DEFAULT_BUFFER_SIZE, once with DX_JOB_ID set and once without, because that constant is fixed at import time.

decisions.label: a
decisions.why: dxfile.py reads dxpy.JOB_ID at import, so each case needs a fresh interpreter. An in-process importlib.reload would re-run the package import and change dxpy module state that other tests in the same process share.

what_it_does: Creates 1005 records with one API call each, resolves 1005 names in batches of 1000, and checks the results at indices 200 and 1003.

decisions.label: a
decisions.why: Create records only at indices 200 and 1003 and pass all 1005 names, since the earlier asserts show a missing name resolves to an empty list. The 1000-entry batch boundary is still crossed, so index 1003 stays in the second batch, and about 1003 create requests per run are removed. Needs the DNAnexus platform.

what_it_does: Resolves a dataset or cohort record, builds a vizserver payload from the filters, sends a raw SQL query and a data query, and compares the SQL and, when data_test is set, the data with expected output.

decisions.label: a
decisions.why: For the three data_test false callers, the data request is the only check that the data endpoint accepts the payload. On an error response VizClient prints it and the results lookup raises KeyError, so skipping the request would turn a failing test into a passing one.

decisions.label: b
decisions.why: Eleven of the 14 calls repeat a record an earlier call resolved, so a module-level dict keyed by record_path can cache the Dataset, cohort_info, and assay name and uuid. The helper reads only those values and no test writes these records, so each skipped call saves a path lookup, a describe, and a visualize request. Needs the DNAnexus platform.

decisions.label: c
decisions.why: The descriptor_file_dict property downloads and decompresses the descriptor file on every access, and lines 1102 and 1103 access it twice for the same two fields. Reading it once removes one DXFile read per call, and the cache in b removes the rest. Needs the DNAnexus platform.

what_it_does: Finds the test project by name, changes the working directory into it, and stores paths and schema references for the class.

decisions.label: a
decisions.why: The _find generator in search.py fetches the next page only when the current page names a next key, and the default first page holds 100 results. For an exact name match list() therefore issues the same single find request as next(iter()), so nothing is saved.

what_it_does: Finds the test project by name, changes the working directory into it, and stores fixture paths for the class.

decisions.label: a
decisions.why: Same as the expression setUpClass: _find fetches a second page only when the first names a next key, so list() makes one request for an exact name match.

what_it_does: Builds a JSONValidator over the shared schema and checks that a malformed filter raises the expected ValueError message.

decisions.label: a
decisions.why: JSONValidator.__init__ only stores the schema and handler and checks that the schema is a non-empty dict, with nothing compiled, so construction costs a few attribute stores. The real work is in validate(), which must run for each input.

what_it_does: Builds a JSONValidator over the shared schema and checks that a valid filter passes validation.

decisions.label: a
decisions.why: JSONValidator.__init__ stores two references and runs one isinstance check, so building a validator per call costs nothing measurable. validate() does the work and must run for this input anyway.

what_it_does: Copies the default parser dict, overrides the given arguments, and checks that ArgsValidator raises the expected message for that combination.

decisions.label: a
decisions.why: ArgsValidator.__init__ stores references and reads one key from the schema, so constructing it costs nothing measurable. validate_input_combination does the work, and it has to run for each case.

what_it_does: Downloads three truth CSVs with dx download into a fresh temp directory and compares them with the output of dx extract_dataset -ddd for one record.

decisions.label: a
decisions.why: Two tests call this function, at lines 41 to 46 and 48 to 53, so each truth file is downloaded twice per run by separate dx download processes. A class-level directory filled on first use and removed in tearDownClass lets both tests share one download with unchanged comparisons, removing three dx CLI starts and their API calls per run. Needs the DNAnexus platform.

what_it_does: Downloads one truth CSV with dx download into a fresh temp directory and compares it with the extracted fields CSV using pandas.

decisions.label: a
decisions.why: Four callers pass two distinct truth files, extract_dataset_test.csv at lines 79 and 98 and Combined_Cohort_Test.csv at lines 88 and 108, so two of the four downloads per run repeat an earlier one. A class-level cache keyed by truth_file, filled on first use, removes those two dx download process starts and their API calls. Needs the DNAnexus platform.

what_it_does: Checks that flatten_json_array turns a multi-line array in a JSON string into the reference single-line form.

decisions.label: a
decisions.why: The discarded call at line 369 runs a few regex passes over one short string, once per run, which is far below what an energy measurement could resolve. Removing it is a fair cleanup, but it saves no measurable energy.

what_it_does: Generates 100 nonces and checks that each has a valid length and appears exactly once in the list.

decisions.label: a
decisions.why: The count inside the loop does about 10 thousand string comparisons in C, well under a millisecond once per run. A set would be faster, but the saving is far below what an energy measurement could resolve.

what_it_does: Runs eight sleeping tasks through response_iterator with four thread pool settings and checks that results come back in order.

decisions.label: a
decisions.why: The sleeps are idle waits that draw idle power only, and their lengths set the completion order the test checks, so shortening them changes what the test exercises.

what_it_does: Runs eight one-second tasks through response_iterator and asserts that task 0 has finished before later tasks start.

decisions.label: a
decisions.why: The one-second sleep keeps each task pending long enough that an overlap would show in pending_tasks, so the assertion depends on it. The cost is idle wait only.

what_it_does: Polls handler.describe every 0.5 s until every stage of an analysis has an executable field, and raises IOError after 200 tries.

decisions.label: a
decisions.why: Each try sends one describe request, and the fixed 0.5 s interval sends about 21 of them in the first 10 s. Doubling the wait up to a 4 s cap, within the same 100 s budget, sends about 5 in that window and returns the same description or raises the same IOError. Needs the DNAnexus platform.

what_it_does: Creates a temp directory, builds an applet in the test project, and builds the workflow spec that embeds that applet ID, before every test method.

decisions.label: a
decisions.why: Ten of the 55 test methods in these classes never read the applet or the spec, so each can skip an applet_new request if both become lazy properties, with a setter on dxworkflow_spec so TestWorkflowBuilderUtils.setUp is unchanged. A scan found no assert on project contents in those ten, though I did not read every line, so the saving is about ten API calls per run and needs the DNAnexus platform.

what_it_does: Resolves the pheno dataset record, builds a raw cohort SQL query from a payload, and checks the SQL against an expected string.

decisions.label: a
decisions.why: This test and test_create_pheno_filter resolve the same record, so a class-level cache filled by whichever runs first saves one resolution per run, which is a path lookup, a describe, and a visualize request. The cached response is only read, so behaviour is unchanged, and the saving is small.

what_it_does: Generates a pheno filter, builds raw cohort SQL from it, creates a cohort record from the filter and SQL, and checks the stored details.

decisions.label: a
decisions.why: It reads the same cached resolution as test_raw_cohort_query_api, so with the shared cache this unit and that one together save a single resolution per run, counted once. Needs the DNAnexus platform.

what_it_does: Copies the local toolkit into a temp applet directory, prepends a pip install line to the entry point, runs dx build on that directory, and removes the temp copy.

decisions.label: a
decisions.why: The copy takes about 29 MB from the repository root, while src/python without its top-level test and doc directories is about 2 MB, and dx build bundles the copy for each of the 11 calls per run. Copying only that subtree keeps the /dxtoolkit/src/python path that the pip install uses, since setup.py reads only files inside src/python, and no other test refers to toolkit paths; this saves about 27 MB of copy and upload per call and needs the DNAnexus platform for the build.
